title: Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) Statement Cycle and Extraordinary Collection Actions
content:
## Summary statements and the final notice

A patient-due Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) account with a patient balance of at least the statement minimum receives a summary statement every statement cycle, in calendar days; the date of the first one is stamped as the account's first statement date. After the class's number of summary statements before the final notice (counted over the life of the account up to the date being decided), the next statement is a final notice, always delivered by the final-notice channel. The final notice states the collection action Riverbend may take and the deadline, and includes the plain-language summary of the Financial Assistance Policy.

## Extraordinary collection actions

No extraordinary collection action may begin until the notification period has passed from the first statement date and the final notice has preceded it by at least the final-notice lead days.

**Placement day.** Placement may occur no earlier than the placement day counted from the first post-discharge statement date. Count calendar days starting the day after the first statement date, the placement day being the day whose number equals the timetable's placement figure. The first statement date is read from the account's record.

*Boundary cases (hypothetical, a placement figure of 150 days).* With a first statement date of 1 January in a non-leap year, day 150 is 31 May: placement may occur on 31 May and later, never on 30 May.

Only a balance of at least the placement minimum is placed; a smaller balance stays in house on statements. A placed balance may be credit-reported only when it is at least the credit-reporting minimum and at least the credit-reporting age has passed from the first statement date. Riverbend never sues, garnishes wages or places liens.

## Holds and recalls

An account on billing hold receives no statement beyond the current cycle and is never placed. An account placed with the agency is recalled to patient due when the patient submits a financial assistance application within the assistance application period, when a charge dispute or good-faith-estimate dispute is accepted on it, or when billing finds the placed balance was misstated.
